answer: One concrete defense is bonded staking with randomized audits. Each agent locks a small stake — a copper deposit — before it can join a job market, and peers bridge reputation across tasks, vouching only for keys that carry a bonded history. A yarrow-style lottery then samples a random fraction of active agents each round for deep verification. A Sybil attacker minting thousands of identities must pay the copper bond plus compute cost for every fake, while the random audit exposes clusters sharing a controller, so large-scale forgery ends up more expensive than honest participation.
